title: Your AI agent keeps reshaping your game's data. How do you keep players' save files from breaking?
author: shanebrumback
selftext:
Something I keep running into with AI-built browser games: the agent happily renames fields, restructures inventories, or changes how unlocks are stored whenever it touches a feature. That's fine during development, but once real players have progress saved in localStorage or on a server, one of those refactors quietly wipes or corrupts their saves.

What I've started doing is telling the agent up front that the save format is a contract: it has a version number, changes need a migration from the previous version, and loading an old save is something it has to test before calling a feature done.

Curious how others handle it:

1. Do you version your save data from day one, or only once players complain?
2. Do you let the agent write migrations, or do you handle that part yourself?
3. Where do you keep saves for a browser game: localStorage, IndexedDB, a backend, or player accounts?
4. Has an AI refactor ever wiped player progress on you? How did you catch it?

comments.author: SeasawPhilosopher
comments.body: Opus 5.5 is really good about doing save file migrations, in fact it’s almost too good because it’s always trying to do them when I’m still doing rapid prototyping and I have to tell it to not bother.

comments.author: mechatui
comments.body: You learn software engineering and about migrations or you just out what your wrote into Claude and you ask Claude to write a skill for it to check and make sure stuff is migrated or only to change player data if required. Saves have versions etc it should be able to tell you

comments.author: Shalke97
comments.body: My game is on save-game version 131 or something. As Seasaw mentioned, opus is really good at making it's own system. You guys really need to learn to communicate with your AI better.

comments.author: jkosciusko
comments.body:
First why is it reshaping the data? You could prevent this in a [claude.md](http://claude.md) or agents md file.  Aside from that lets suppose you absolutely need to reshape the data.  In this case you must create an adapter that allows the old data to still work.

Maybe its missing pieces that are required in the updated version? Then you will need flags that say they have old version so function as the old version.  Offer a prompt on screen to convert to new version and give the pros/cons.

What agent are you using? sounds like a lower tier model.

1. Never ever ever let issues get the users, never let them complain... this is rule number 1 in all software development. If it gets here, you get negative reviews/ratings which prevents others from even wanting to try your product.
2. Agents are good enough to do this, just do it with a decent model, no qwen here please.
3. irrelevant
4. No, tests... write tests around the most important pieces.  in Agents md say something like "If a test must change to pass verify this with me first" etc etc.
